quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #21
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 19

questions.question: You are driving on a highway with two solid yellow lines. You may:

options.text: Cross these lines only to turn left into or from an alley, private road, or driveway.
Cross these lines to pass other vehicles if there is no oncoming traffic.
Cross these lines only to make a U-turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cross these lines only to turn left into or from an alley, private road, or driveway.
questions.explanation: Double solid yellow lines mean you cannot pass other vehicles from either direction. You can only cross these lines to turn left into or from an alley, private road, or driveway.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.explanation: This sign tells drivers which direction to drive on a one-way street. It shows you must follow the direction the arrow points.

questions.question: When two vehicles enter an intersection at the same time from different roads, who must yield?
questions.explanation: When two vehicles arrive at an intersection at the same time, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right. This rule applies at all intersections.

questions.question: When visibility is poor, what should you do first?

options.text: Look for road edge markings to guide you.

questions.explanation: Your first action when visibility decreases should be to slow down. This helps you stay safe in dangerous conditions.

questions.question: You are in the left lane and want to move to the right lane. You should:

options.text: Check your mirrors, signal, and look over your left shoulder before changing lanes.
Check your mirrors, signal, and look over your right shoulder before changing lanes.
Check your mirrors, signal, and look over both shoulders before changing lanes.
Check your mirrors, signal, and change lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your mirrors, signal, and look over your right shoulder before changing lanes.
questions.explanation: Always check your mirrors and turn on your signal before changing lanes. Look over your shoulder in the direction you want to move to check your blind spot.

questions.question: When changing lanes, you should:

options.text: Signal as you move into the next lane.
Signal 500 feet ahead on residential streets.

questions.explanation: Cars and motorcycles can hide in your blind spot. Always look over your shoulder before changing lanes. Signal 100 feet ahead on residential streets or 5 seconds ahead on a freeway.

questions.question: What does this black and yellow sign mean?

options.text: The road to the right is one-way only.
There is a detour to the right due to roadwork.
Slow down because the road ahead makes a sharp turn.
There is a crossroad to your right.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down because the road ahead makes a sharp turn.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that the road ahead makes a sharp turn in the direction shown. Slow down before the curve, just as you would at an intersection.

questions.question: When parking uphill on a hill with a curb, how should you turn your front wheels?

options.text: Turn them sharply toward the curb.
Turn them slightly to the right.
Turn them sharply away from the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn them sharply away from the curb.
questions.explanation: Turn your wheels sharply away from the curb when parking uphill. This stops your car from rolling into traffic if your brakes fail.

questions.question: When you approach a railroad crossing with no warning lights or gates, you should:

options.text: Cross the tracks as quickly as possible.
Always stop before crossing the tracks.
Be ready to yield to any train.
Speed up to beat any oncoming train.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready to yield to any train.
questions.explanation: Always be prepared to yield to trains at any crossing. Do not cross until your entire vehicle can clear the tracks. Do not shift gears while crossing to avoid stalling.

questions.question: Your body processes approximately how much alcohol per hour?
questions.explanation: Your body processes about one alcoholic drink per hour. How impaired you become depends on how much you drink, how fast you drink it, your body weight, whether you have eaten, and your overall health.

questions.question: A small vehicle may start to float in only ____ of water.
questions.explanation: Do not drive through flooded areas. A small vehicle can start to float in only six inches of water. Deeper water can wash a vehicle away.

questions.question: You may cross double solid yellow lines:
questions.explanation: Double solid lines mean you cannot pass or change lanes. You can only cross them to turn left into or out of a driveway, or to make a U-turn where allowed.

questions.question: A single broken yellow line down the center of a two-lane road means:

options.text: Traffic moves in opposite directions. Drivers cannot pass.
Traffic moves in opposite directions. Drivers can pass when safe.
Traffic moves in the same direction. Drivers cannot pass.
Traffic moves in the same direction. Drivers can pass when safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic moves in opposite directions. Drivers can pass when safe.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions. A dashed yellow line means drivers next to it can pass when it is safe to do so.

questions.question: As a pedestrian, you should:

options.text: Always have the right-of-way over vehicles in a crosswalk.
Never enter a street or crosswalk when vehicles are close.
Enter a crosswalk anytime because drivers must stop.
Use crosswalks only when it is convenient.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never enter a street or crosswalk when vehicles are close.
questions.explanation: Do not enter a street or crosswalk when vehicles are close. Even though pedestrians have the right-of-way in crosswalks, a nearby vehicle may not have time to stop.

questions.question: Leave extra space between your vehicle and others when stopping:
questions.explanation: Leave more space in front of your vehicle when stopped on an uphill slope. If the car ahead rolls backward when traffic starts moving, extra space helps prevent a collision.

questions.question: The most important thing about speed and curves is that you must:

options.text: Drive at the speed limit as you enter the curve, then slow down at the sharpest part.
Slow down before you enter the curve.
Speed up gently before you enter the curve.
Drive at the speed limit before, during, and after the curve.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down before you enter the curve.
questions.explanation: Slow down before entering a curve. Your vehicle's weight can make turning difficult. You must reduce speed to stay in control.

questions.question: In good driving conditions, keep at least ____ between your vehicle and the car ahead.
questions.explanation: In good conditions, keep three to four seconds between your vehicle and the one ahead. On wet or slippery roads, use at least four seconds. In poor conditions, increase your distance even more.

questions.question: When you see a stopped school bus with flashing lights, you must stop:
questions.explanation: On all roads and driveways, traffic from both directions must stop before reaching a stopped school bus with red flashing lights.

questions.question: Signs that require drivers to follow an instruction are called:
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs require drivers to obey them. Breaking the rules on these signs can result in a penalty.

questions.question: Pentagonal signs show:
questions.explanation: Pentagonal signs mark school zones. Drive carefully in these areas and watch for children and pedestrians.

questions.question: What is a safe way to drive through a curve?

options.text: Slow down when you enter the curve. Speed up when you exit.
Keep the same speed the whole time.
Speed up when you enter the curve. Slow down when you exit.
Stay near the right edge of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down when you enter the curve. Speed up when you exit.
questions.explanation: Slow down as you enter a curve. Gradually speed up as you exit. Speeding up when entering a curve makes it harder to control your vehicle.

questions.question: What color are most warning signs?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are diamond-shaped and yellow with black markings. They alert drivers to unexpected conditions on the road ahead.

questions.question: What color are road markings that separate traffic going in opposite directions?
questions.explanation: Yellow lines in the center of the road separate traffic moving in opposite directions.

questions.question: What is true about a work zone?

options.text: It can be moving or stationary.
It is marked with black and white signs.
You do not need to slow down or pay extra attention.

questions.correctAnswerText: It can be moving or stationary.
questions.explanation: Work zones can be stationary or moving, such as vehicles striping lines, mowing, or removing snow. Orange signs with black letters mark work zones. Always slow down and pay close attention when you enter a work zone.

questions.question: A driver ahead does not dim their bright headlights. Where should you look?

options.text: At the wheels of the oncoming vehicle.
To the right side of the road.
To the left side of the road.
Straight ahead down the middle of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: To the right side of the road.
questions.explanation: Look toward the right side of the road. This keeps you from being blinded by the bright lights and lets you see the road well enough to stay in your lane until the other vehicle passes.
